messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — compliance asked for FIPS-certified container images for a regulated customer. The blocker: upstream OpenSSL backports + a glibc microfix we need to include. Who can own prioritization?

jordan: We should treat FIPS images as a separate image stream (ubuntu-fips / alpine-fips). Priorities: 1) ubuntu-fips x86_64, 2) ubuntu-fips aarch64, 3) alpine-fips. Keep canaries small. :+1:

liam: Agree on stream separation. Need to confirm whether the OpenSSL ABI changes require rebuilds of downstream libs. Quick check: `ldd /usr/lib/libssl.so` differences could break some images.

maya: Good call. Sara, any compliance constraints on signing/attestations for these images? KMS key usage?

sara: Yes — images must be signed with our FIPS-approved KMS key and attestations stored in audit-log (retention 2y). RBAC: only security-sre and release-engineering roles can sign. We also need enrollment docs for the customer.

liam: For the build pipeline, proposal: add a `fips=true` build flag and a separate `image-signer` step that calls our KMS. Sketch:```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y openssl=3.2.x-fips glibc-patch
LABEL redwood.fips=true
```
then: `./tools/image-signer sign --kms-key projects/redwood/keys/fips-sign`

jordan: Test matrix suggestion: canary on staging, then 3% of dedicated pool for 24h, then ramp. Add smoke tests for: TLS handshakes, grpc clients, startup/compat tests. Capture token-level latency and truth-set for TLS.

maya: Risk notes: alpine builds may not be FIPS-certified upstream; we may need to drop alpine-fips if vendor refuses. Also watch for `glibc` symbol versions — we may need to pin old ABI or build with `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` off to avoid regressions.

sara: Action items: I will create an IAM role for `image-signer` with `signBlob` permission and scope it to the FIPS key. I'll add audit log alerting for any non-release principal using sign.

jordan: Who owns the rebuild? liam? If so we need a timeline. Also: add an automated smoke test that runs `openssl s_server` + cert validation against a known client in CI.

liam: I can drive the rebuild. Timeline: prototype image and canary pipeline by EOW (Fri), full canary early next week. Need one other reviewer for ABI/regression testing — @maya?

maya: I can review the security/signing bits and help with audit retention tests. Will set up a quick checklist in the security repo.

devops-bot: Deploy job queued: `image-build/ubuntu-fips/1855554321` triggered by liam. Canary window reserved: 2026-04-06 02:00 -> 2026-04-06 06:00 UTC.

staging-ci: Canary test run scheduled. Tests: tls-handshake, grpc-smoke, startup-time, auth-integration. Reporting to #eng-sre.

jordan: One more note — include image attestation (in-toto/SLSA) in registry metadata and a signed SBOM. Compliance will require SBOM per release.

maya: Great. Sara can you add the RBAC policy change to the release playbook and get it approved?

sara: On it. I'll open a PR with policy and link to the KMS key. Also adding an alert for `sign` events outside release windows.

liam: I'll open the rebuild PR and tag reviewers. Plan: detect any ABI/regressions in 24h canary, rollback if TLS handshake fails or startup regresses >200ms median.

maya: Thanks team. If anyone hits a blocking CVE or regression during canary, post here and @sara + @jordan. :eyes:

devops-bot: Canary health check: queued. Will post results to this thread when done.
